resources.title: Vocal imitation in parrots: addressing specific individuals
resources.task: Understand what a targeted contact-call playback can establish about receiver response and what it cannot establish about meaning.
resources.review_depth: Reviewed the full primary PLOS article text for the abstract, introduction, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, Ethics Statement and article license. No raw recordings, associated dataset, supplementary material or analysis code were acquired or inspected; no reanalysis was performed.
resources.access: Open full-text PLOS article; associated recordings, dataset, supplementary materials and code were not checked or acquired.
resources.decision: Use as a controlled signal-function comparator. Do not treat as evidence of translation, a companion-parrot result or support for consumer-app playback.
resources.limitations: This was a controlled playback study of 36 wild-caught orange-fronted conures from 27 flocks, paired in short-term outdoor aviaries during 2007. Of 72 trial periods, 44 were retained for analysis after caller-assignment and outside-interaction exclusions. The authors report higher call rates and shorter response latency for the targeted bird overall, with a sex-specific call-rate pattern; non-target birds also responded. This supports a bounded, context-specific receiver response to acoustically targeted imitation, not decoding of sentence meaning, general conversation, or a result transferable to pet parrots, other species or phone speakers. The experiment used captured birds, repeated playback and video observation under research permits. No Talk2Nature replication or independent specialist review exists.
resources.attribution: Balsby, Momberg and Dabelsteen (2012), PLOS ONE 7(11): e49747, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0049747.

rights.license: Creative Commons Attribution License (version not stated on the reviewed PLOS article page)
rights.scope: Published article text only. The current article page does not identify a license version. Raw recordings, trial-level data, figures, supplements and code have not been separately assessed.
rights.conditions: Attribute the authors and source and indicate adaptations. Verify the applicable license version before reusing article material; Talk2Nature publishes an original summary and link and reproduces no figures.

resources.title: Predicting interaction context in captive Egyptian fruit bats
resources.version: EUSIPCO 2024, pp. 1277–1281; arXiv author manuscript v1: 2406.06332
resources.task: Reproducibility and evaluation-split comparator for context prediction from bat ultrasound calls.
resources.review_depth: Reviewed the complete official five-page EUSIPCO proceedings paper and arXiv v1 record/manuscript, including dataset filtering, subject-independent test-fold description, random train/validation split, models, metrics, results, errors and license record. No code, split files, data media, model weights or supplementary artifacts were acquired or run.
resources.access: Official EUSIPCO proceedings PDF and versioned arXiv v1 manuscript; article PDFs were reviewed in the browser only.
resources.decision: Prior-art and reproducibility comparator. The paper already reports subject-independent context-prediction folds; consider only an exact reproduction or a reviewer-justified robustness audit, not a novel benchmark or translation result.
resources.limitations: The paper reports three subject-independent development/test folds, but the exact partition files, identity/group definitions, session overlap and channel/treatment balance have not been independently verified. Its 70/30 train/validation split within each development set is stratified random and does not account for identity. The reported sample-bootstrap confidence intervals are not group-clustered. Grooming recall is zero, context labels are video-derived, and no public code or split artifact was located in the targeted review despite the paper's statement that code would be released upon acceptance. Rechecked 2026-10-29 from official primary sources: the paper reports subject-independent development/test folds, so another caller-held-out result is not novel by itself. Exact fold membership and both interaction-role/session/chamber controls remain unverified; no Talk2Nature split or reproduction exists.

resources.review_depth: Rechecked the official eLife version-of-record Table 1, Methods and Data Availability, plus its public peer-review/author-response page on October 28. The article points all tables and code to Mendeley Data v1. The Methods mention a lower-rate 2-click/min repeat and bat playback only in a separate flight-response hearing check after deafening; Table 1 reports no outcome row for the 2-click/min condition and no Bat oviposition condition. No source mapping explains the workbook's Bat egg-cluster label. The Mendeley Data v1 landing page, published 2025-11-14, declares CC0 1.0. One approved 51,160-byte data.xlsx file was acquired to ignored local storage on October 24 and its SHA-256 matches the exact value displayed in the file panel. A standard-library aggregate-only audit matched all five main Table 1 repetition, paired-observation and egg-cluster totals. No formulas or deposited code were executed. The other 31 listed files and separate eLife source-data ZIP remain unacquired; no inferential model or independent review was completed.
resources.access: The exact data.xlsx file UUID and public download URL are pinned in observed_inventory. A TLS-verified HEAD to the Mendeley URL returned 302 to the pinned public S3 object; a HEAD to that exact object returned HTTP 200, 51,160 bytes and XLSX MIME type. The local collector fetched only that file, verified its SHA-256 against the Mendeley file-panel value, and wrote a receipt under ignored local storage. The official API reference marks file-list/download APIs OAuth2-protected; no API client or token was used. This acquisition covers one spreadsheet only; the other 31 files and publisher ZIP remain separate and unacquired.
resources.decision: Retain only the version-pinned data.xlsx and receipt in ignored external storage for bounded local structure and aggregate-table review. The aggregate audit may be shared with its method and limitations, but do not publish raw rows, acquire the full archive, execute unreviewed code, use this behavioral table for model training or private storage, or treat it as evidence for general plant communication. Exclude the lower-rate and Bat workbook conditions from the reported oviposition outcomes; the Bat row remains unexplained by the source record.
resources.limitations: The deposit concerns one controlled study of Egyptian cotton leafworm moths and tomato-plant playback. The selected spreadsheet is behavioral/source data, not an audio corpus, and does not reproduce the paper's hierarchical models or adjusted contrasts. All five main Table 1 aggregate tuples match, but that is a source-table consistency check rather than independent reproduction. The lower-rate 2-click/min label is mentioned in Methods but has no Table 1 outcome row. Bat playback in the version of record is a separate flight-response hearing check after deafening; no source mapping links it to the workbook's Bat oviposition label. Keep both extra labels outside the reported outcomes. A bounded reanalysis would not establish plant intention, general communication, animal translation or model readiness. No Talk2Nature specialist review is established by acquisition.

resources.decision: Use the paper to frame testable alternatives, not as evidence that either theory is confirmed. Minimal Compositionality predicts that separate ABC and D calls may still support mobbing when linked to the same event, though less readily than ABC–D; Bird Implicatures predicts a standalone call can imply the fuller combination is false and block mobbing. Seek expert review before proposing an animal-facing test.
resources.limitations: This is a theoretical synthesis of earlier receiver studies, not a new playback experiment, dataset, code release or independent empirical replication. The accounts differ in auxiliary assumptions: Minimal Compositionality requires an event-like existential meaning for D, while Bird Implicatures requires ABC–D to be an evoked alternative and uses a receiver-centered version to address the hybrid sequence. Both can accommodate the reported source-separation result. The publisher supplement was not separately reviewed; appendices in the HAL manuscript were not fully recalculated.

resources.decision: Metadata-only. Keep this as an evidence and schema reference. If official file access becomes available and a defined analysis is justified, inspect only the small measurement, selection-table and site-level files locally, preserve site-year grouping, and keep training admission false.
resources.limitations: The deposit contains processed call measurements and metadata, not raw audio or roost-count data. Its 2,461-call selection table and 2,461-row acoustic table use human-assigned call-type labels; BirdID is unique only within a site-year, so call-level random splits risk site/year leakage. No inter-annotator reliability statistic was found in the reviewed paper/protocol. The rendered page reports 109.8 GB while the nine-file API manifest totals 3,546,609,904 bytes; unresolved. UNKNOWN is not a stable class.

resources.title: V33DA: physically verified zebra-finch caller-attribution benchmark
resources.task: Candidate first technical task: attribute a detected, isolated vocalization to one of the visible birds using audio/video/pose, with caller truth derived from on-body accelerometer data. This is caller attribution, not call meaning or reply detection.
resources.review_depth: Reviewed the complete pinned dataset card and code/sample README plus included metadata.json and split_summary.json. Computed verified-TLS SHA-256 hashes in memory for those three text files and matched their Git blob IDs; see research/v33da_sample_manifest.json. The complete sample-only Git tree lists 334 files (62,503,976 bytes), including 100 audio, accelerometer and video files. No Parquet, media, executable code or model bytes were acquired or run.
resources.access: No binary sample, Parquet, audio, accelerometer, video or calibration bytes were acquired. Three small text files were fetched in memory only, checksummed against the pinned Git tree and not retained locally.
resources.decision: Keep metadata-only. Dataset card and nested sample README declare CC BY 4.0; repository MIT license applies to software. The 62.5 MB sample exceeds the collector 20 MiB per-invocation limit. The full-release held-out BP05 set comprises three unseen physical callers but also changes experiment, group, date/year and cage; treat it as a bundled shift test. No acquisition or model run is authorized by this review.
resources.limitations: Caller identity is not behavior, addressee, receiver response, intent or meaning. The full release comes from one aviary/recording geometry and excludes overlapping calls. The experiment-held-out split tests three unseen BP05 callers (brown 56 events, purple 2,140, yellow 3,633) but bundles experiment, group, date/year and cage changes; event counts are not independent sample size. A session split retains the same physical birds. Leave-one-bird-out is advertised but exact implementation/fold membership is unverified. The 100-event sample has no verified sample-specific split or Parquet join. BP05 metadata includes an extra red color without an event-count group; candidate-set membership and chance baseline remain unknown. No media or Parquet bytes were inspected.
resources.attribution: Basha, M. et al. (2026), Who Called? V33DA: A Physically Verified Multimodal Benchmark for Vocal Attribution in Zebra Finch Groups; associated manuscript listed as under review in the dataset card.

Treat precise locations as potentially sensitive wildlife-location information; keep public geography coarse and exclude coordinates from derivatives unless an appropriate review establishes a need and safe handling. Its contents were not reviewed; no other provider hash was recomputed. Annotation values, grouping keys and the split were not inspected. The 2025 paper already trains a ViT metric-learning model on this corpus and uses embeddings for repertoire similarity and demographic song-culture analysis; no distinct Talk2Nature task has been approved. resources.review_depth: Official DCASE 2018 task description, dataset partition guidance, metrics and results; Stowell et al. resources.decision: Promote to the strongest current task-match lead for passive bird-sound presence detection, ahead of ArcticBirdSounds for the specific binary-presence question. Do not select it as a Talk2Nature benchmark or begin acquisition/training until a qualified reviewer checks label scope, component rights, independent grouping, held-out-label access and a reproducible modern baseline.

Bird presence is not equivalent to a bounded call-event label. Public development data do not provide a single untouched locked test after all three domains have informed development; the challenge evaluation audio is public but evaluation labels were kept private and are absent from the reviewed Zenodo record. Challenge page states CC BY 4.0 for all datasets, but the evaluation deposit shows no license value and source-level rights still require reconciliation. The legacy baseline is Python 2.7/Theano/Lasagne, has no license file visible in the top-level repository listing, and the README estimates about 30 GPU-hours for the full system. resources.review_depth: Targeted full-text review of the five-page v1 preprint: abstract, dataset construction, caption and split design, generation method, evaluation, results, conclusion and ethics statement. resources.decision: Record as recent generation prior art, not a communication capability or product model. Preserve Talk2Nature's zero-command boundary: do not integrate generated calls into observation tools or play generated audio to animals. Its paper metrics evaluate vocalization-anchor discriminability and distribution fidelity, not whether an animal understands or responds to a prompt.
resources.limitations: The six-species BeVo set has 31,191 events and 42 anchors. Samples are stratified and randomly split within species/anchor; the reviewed paper does not describe animal-, source-recording- or site-held-out evaluation. GPT-5.6 creates 500 conditions per anchor from literature-derived behavior cards; the authors report no manual post-generation verification. Conditions attach to groups sharing an anchor, not verified behavior for each recording. Test text uses new formulations of behavioral knowledge already represented during training, not unseen behaviors. Classifier shifts and audio-distribution metrics do not establish semantic grounding, animal comprehension, sender intent or receiver response. This is an unreviewed preprint with no independent Talk2Nature reproduction.

resources.title: Oyster-fungus electrical recordings dataset
resources.version: Zenodo record 4430968 v1; published 2021-01-10; API updated 2026-10-18
resources.task: Methods and reproducibility context for slow, multichannel extracellular fungal electrical recordings; not an animal-audio resource or evidence of linguistic communication.
resources.review_depth: Reviewed the primary paper's data-availability statement and publisher-indexed Methods for the reported sampling rate, event threshold and propagation window; direct article navigation was blocked by the publisher cookie gate. Also reviewed the official Zenodo landing page/API metadata and license documentation, and the ZIP end record/central-directory metadata using exact HTTPS byte ranges. The landing-page License row appears empty. Read 83,371 bytes of archive metadata only. The 80 file entries comprise 18 CSVs, 19 TARs and 43 JPEGs; 13 CSVs are at least 20 MB. No file payload was read; the API MD5 was not verified against the archive.
resources.access: The primary paper cites this DOI for its approximately fifteen-day, eight-channel, 1 Hz recording from one oyster-fungus specimen. The 2021 ZIP directory identifies multiple large CSV candidates and nested TAR files but does not identify the analyzed series. No filename clearly identifies a license/readme/notice member; nested TAR contents were not inspected.
resources.decision: Keep metadata-only. The Zenodo API declares record-level CC BY 4.0 while the landing page's Rights > License row appears empty; the outer ZIP has no named rights/readme notice and possible nested component rights remain unreviewed. The paper-to-record DOI link is verified, but the series is not mapped among 13 large CSV candidates. Establish file-level rights and define a justified target with qualified electrophysiology review before opening member payloads, analysis or redistribution.
resources.limitations: The study uses eight channels from one specimen; channels are not independent biological replicates. The saved signal is one averaged value per second, and the paper uses a fixed baseline +2 SD event threshold, 60-second minimum duration and 300-second cross-channel window; findings are limited to slow dynamics and these analysis choices. Temporal propagation does not establish a vocabulary, receiver, referent or communication. The paper reports shuffled-train controls, but independent replication and substrate, electrode and environmental controls remain open. No audio-language model or phone microphone is suitable for this electrophysiology dataset.

resources.task: Prior-method implementation for ecological bird-vocalization detection; not a validated Talk2Nature baseline.
resources.review_depth: GitHub repository page, README, visible folder list and repository-level MIT license indicator reviewed. No code, dependency file, training data, model or tests were inspected or run.
resources.access: Public repository metadata; exact revision was not pinned or acquired.
resources.decision: Keep metadata only. Before reproduction, pin a commit, inspect code and dependencies, map each input and output, and check source-data and checkpoint rights separately.
resources.limitations: A repository-level MIT indicator does not establish licenses for linked or embedded datasets, model weights, dependencies or the preprint. Current branch may change; no independent reproduction or security review was performed.
resources.attribution: Christin et al. author-linked repository, Vin985/BioSoundNet, default branch main as viewed 2026-10-31.

rights.license: MIT displayed at repository level; exact commit and file scope not pinned in this review.
rights.scope: Repository code only, subject to the exact license text and any file-level or third-party notices; excludes paper, data, weights and dependencies unless separately covered.
rights.conditions: Pin the exact commit; retain applicable MIT notice; audit dependencies, bundled assets, data inputs and checkpoint licensing before execution, redistribution or commercial use.

rights.license: Unverified; repository-level MIT status does not establish checkpoint-specific terms or scope.

resources.title: Software tools for passive acoustic monitoring: a living systematic review
resources.task: Prior-art and interoperability reference for selecting an open, maintainable role for Talk2Nature among existing bioacoustic and ecoacoustic tools.
resources.review_depth: Reviewed the article abstract, Methods §§2.1–2.3, Results §§3.1–3.2, conclusion, data availability, article license and three public reviewer reports. No supplementary files or tools were acquired or run.
resources.access: Open Version 1 article and public review reports; the article declares CC BY 4.0 for article content.
resources.decision: Use as a dated landscape and design reference. Quote counts only with the section and the article's internal discrepancies disclosed. Prioritize a verified interoperability need over another end-to-end platform.
resources.limitations: Literature ends 2024-01-01. The article's abstract and main text differ on PAM-dedicated tool and full-workflow counts. Public reviewers request direct software links, more granular features, clearer screening detail and a supportable living-update procedure. This is not an independent current feature audit or user study.
resources.attribution: Hanf-Dressler et al. (2026), F1000Research 15:48, Version 1, DOI 10.12688/f1000research.173495.1; cite the article separately from its linked inventory and R script.

rights.license: CC BY 4.0 declared for the article.
rights.scope: Article text only. The OSF inventory and R analysis script are separately cataloged and have a different rights-verification record.
rights.conditions: Attribute the article and indicate adaptations; do not reproduce third-party works or infer rights for the supplementary files from the article license.

resources.title: Ecoacoustic software inventory, PRISMA materials and dendrogram
resources.version: Public OSF project v72ce; API metadata modified 2025-11-20
resources.task: Potential structured tool inventory for interoperability and coverage comparison; not a Talk2Nature benchmark or field dataset.
resources.review_depth: The paper's data-availability statement lists ECOACOUSTIC_SOFTWARE_INVENTORY.xlsx, an interactive dendrogram, PRISMA materials and an R script. The official OSF node API confirmed the public project title, summary and modified date, but its root license field is null. No file manifest, individual license field or payload was read.
resources.access: Public OSF project metadata and DOI; the linked individual files were not opened or acquired.
resources.decision: Metadata only. Use the paper's own summarized findings for now. Before file-level reuse, inspect the exact version, manifest, item-level terms and included software links.
resources.limitations: The inventory reflects a literature frame through 2023 and tool availability at analysis time, not a current 2026 census. The article states CC0 for its underlying package, but the current OSF root API exposes no license value; the exact item-level scope was not checked. Do not assume the article's CC BY 4.0 applies to these files.
resources.attribution: Hanf-Dressler et al. (2026) article data deposit, OSF project v72ce, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/V72CE; cite the article and deposit separately.

rights.license: Article states CC0 for the underlying data package; OSF project API license is null; item-level terms remain unverified.
rights.scope: Spreadsheet inventory, PRISMA materials and dendrogram named by the article; individual contents and embedded links may have separate terms.
rights.conditions: Verify exact file version and rights before download, reuse, redistribution or commercial analysis; preserve the provenance and tool-level license data separately.

resources.title: R analysis script for the ecoacoustic software review
resources.version: Named in the F1000Research Version 1 data-availability statement; exact file revision not inspected
resources.task: Potential reproducibility reference for the article's inventory analysis and figures; not Talk2Nature production code.
resources.review_depth: The article identifies PAM_SOFTWARE_ANALYSIS.R as the analysis script on OSF and says the underlying package is CC0. The OSF project root currently has license=null. The file, dependencies and code-level notices were not inspected or run.
resources.access: Public OSF project DOI; no script payload acquired.
resources.decision: Metadata only. If reproduction is justified, pin the file version and hash, inspect its dependencies and exact license, and compare its declared outputs with the article before execution.
resources.limitations: The paper's CC0 statement and null OSF root license need item-level reconciliation; project-level access does not establish safe code execution, dependency rights or reproducibility. No run has been performed.
resources.attribution: Hanf-Dressler et al. (2026), analysis script named in the Version 1 article's Data Availability statement; OSF project v72ce.

rights.license: Article states CC0 for underlying files; OSF root API license is null and the exact script-file license was not verified.
rights.scope: Analysis script and any dependencies; separate from article text, inventory data and software entries in the inventory.
rights.conditions: Verify exact script and dependency terms; inspect source before running and retain original provenance.

resources.title: The audience shapes the information content of the honey bee waggle dance
resources.task: Primary evidence for a species-bounded communication question: whether receiver availability changes precision in a known referential signal.
resources.review_depth: Full article reviewed through the official PNAS/PMC record, including experiments, controls, results, discussion, data statement and article license. No supplementary file or media acquired.
resources.access: Open-access article under CC BY 4.0. Its dataset is deposited separately on Zenodo; no software or model artifact was reviewed.
resources.decision: Use as prior art and a methods reference. The observed audience effect is already published; any Talk2Nature work should first test whether a transparent reproduction or distinct question is justified.
resources.limitations: The result concerns honey bee waggle-dance precision under the studied audience manipulations. It is not a general animal-language result and does not validate transfer to other species or settings.
resources.attribution: Lin T, Dong S, Gu G, Zhang F, Ye X, Wang T, Wang Z, Li J, Nieh JC, Chittka L, Tan K (2026). The audience shapes the information content of the honey bee waggle dance. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 123(14): e2518687123. DOI 10.1073/pnas.2518687123.

rights.license: CC-BY-4.0
rights.scope: Published article only; the separate dataset and any software or model artifacts have distinct rights.
rights.conditions: Attribute the authors and source, link the license and indicate changes if article material is reused. Talk2Nature publishes an original summary and source link.

resources.title: Honey bee audience-feedback experiment data

resources.review_depth: Official Zenodo v1 record and API metadata reviewed. One XLSX file is listed (109,830 bytes; MD5 1adc5aefa26c1d7a49e6395f678a240d); the payload was not downloaded, locally hashed or inspected.
resources.access: Public Zenodo metadata record. The record lists a single XLSX data file; no supplementary media or code is included in this catalog record.
resources.decision: Metadata only, not acquired and not training-ready. Before any data inspection or reproduction, reviewers must verify the workbook-to-paper mapping, independent experimental units, nesting, and whether a prespecified result can be reproduced. No ML benchmark is selected.
resources.limitations: The file contents, data dictionary, trial/colony structure and location fields have not been checked. Record-level licensing does not establish anything about associated article, code, dependency or model rights.
resources.attribution: Lin T et al. (2026). Data for The audience shapes the information content of the honey bee waggle dance. Zenodo v1. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10892587.

rights.license: Zenodo v1 official API metadata declares CC BY 4.0 for the deposited dataset.
rights.scope: Dataset record only. The associated paper, software, dependencies and model artifacts require separate rights review.
rights.conditions: Retain attribution to the deposit. Review the exact file and scientific suitability before any acquisition or analysis; no dataset bytes have been inspected.
